months.note: 일부는 사철 머물며 번식하고, 겨울에는 북쪽 번식 무리가 중부 이남으로 내려와 수가 늘어난다. 산란은 4~7월.

summary: 숲이 우거진 산골짜기의 계곡과 냇가에 사는 작은 오리다. 물가에 가까운 오래된 나무의 구멍이나 바위틈에 둥지를 틀고, 도토리 같은 나무 열매와 수서곤충, 작은 물고기를 먹는다. 국내에서는 일부가 텃새로 사철 머물며, 겨울에는 북쪽에서 내려온 무리가 더해져 저수지와 하천에 모인다. 천연기념물로 지정되어 보호받는다.

points.en: red bill with a whitish tip
broad white crescent above the eye
two white bars on the purple breast

sexes.male: 번식깃 수컷은 붉은 부리(끝은 흰색), 눈 위의 넓은 흰 반달무늬, 주황빛 뺨과 목의 장식깃, 흰 세로줄 두 개가 든 보랏빛 가슴, 등 위로 세운 주황색 돛 모양 깃을 갖춰 다른 오리와 혼동되지 않는다. 번식이 끝나면 암컷과 비슷한 에클립스깃으로 바뀌지만 부리는 붉은색으로 남는다.
sexes.female: 전체적으로 어두운 회갈색이고 몸 아랫면에 흰 얼룩점이 흩어져 있다. 머리는 회색으로, 눈 둘레의 흰 테가 눈 뒤로 가늘게 이어진다. 부리는 검고 끝이 연한 색이다.

similar.how: 암컷끼리 견주면 청둥오리 암컷은 갈색 얼룩 바탕에 어두운 눈선이 눈을 가로지르고 부리에 주황색이 섞인다. 원앙 암컷은 머리가 회색이고, 흰 눈테가 눈 뒤의 가는 흰 선으로 이어진다.

art.subject: Mandarin Duck (Aix galericulata), adult male in full breeding plumage, as seen in Korea from October to May: small bright red bill with a whitish nail; broad white crescent sweeping back from above the eye to the nape; dark glossy green-purple forehead and crown running into a long drooping crest that turns chestnut-orange at the rear; orange-buff face with elongated orange hackles fanning down the sides of the neck; deep purple-maroon breast with two vertical white bars bordered by black on its side; golden orange-buff flanks; a pair of large upright orange sail feathers raised above the back; dark olive-brown back; white belly and undertail; dark eye; orange-yellow legs.
art.pose: Floating on calm water in clear side profile with the orange sails raised, a quiet ripple around the body.
art.scene: A shaded pool of a mountain stream in a Korean deciduous forest in late autumn: overhanging oak and maple branches with a few remaining yellow and orange leaves, mossy boulders along the bank, fallen leaves and acorns drifting on the still water, soft reflections of the trees. No people, buildings or text.
views: adult male, breeding plumage, swimming, side view: red bill with whitish tip, broad white crescent above the eye, long chestnut-and-green crest, orange neck hackles, purple breast with two white bars edged black, orange-buff flanks, upright orange sails

adult female, swimming, side view: grey head with a white eye-ring continuing as a thin white line behind the eye, white at the bill base and chin, dark grey bill with a pale tip, olive-brown back, brownish breast and flanks spotted with white
eclipse male, swimming, side view: female-like grey-brown plumage without crest, sails or neck hackles, but the bill still bright red
art.build: Small, compact perching duck, about 45cm, noticeably smaller than a Mallard, with a large-headed look from the crest and a short neck. Bill short and narrow, much shorter than the head, with a broad pale nail. Legs short, orange-yellow in the male and dull yellowish in the female. Tail rather long for a duck, held low. Perches readily on branches and rocks over water and nests in tree holes.
avoid: Do not paint a red eye, a red eye-ring or a green crested head with thin white lines; that is the American Wood Duck (Aix sponsa).
Do not lay the orange sails flat or leave them out on the breeding male; they stand upright above the back.
Do not give the female a dark eye-stripe or an orange-marked bill like a female Mallard; she has a grey head and white spectacles.
Do not paint the female's bill red; only the male's bill is red.
